en.title: Why the Boeing 777-9 is not a straight replacement for every Airbus A380
en.summary: The A380, built from 2003 to 2021, typically seats 500–600 passengers and still has no direct replacement; the 777-9 typically seats about 400–430 but burns roughly 2,600 gallons of fuel per hour against the A380's roughly 4,600. The 777-9 wins on twin-engine efficiency and flexibility, replacing the A380's role in a network rather than its seat count flight for flight.
body: The Airbus A380 was manufactured from 2003 until 2021 and remains the highest-capacity commercial jet ever produced, with no direct replacement available on the open market. Typical layouts hold 500 to 600 seats; the densest example operated by Emirates carried 615, and Airbus lists a maximum certified capacity of 853 seats. The closest successors, high-capacity variants of the Airbus A350 and Boeing 777 families, approach but do not exceed 500 seats. The Boeing 777-9 typically seats around 400 to 430 in a multi-cabin layout. Korean Air once flew a 407-seat all-business-class A380, reported by Flight Global in 2018, but that was an exceptional charter configuration. Whatever the configuration, the A380 offers more floor area and a higher certified maximum capacity than the 777-9, so the seats once carried on an A380 route cannot be transferred evenly onto a 777-9.

The seat-count gap is offset by fuel efficiency. The 777-9's two General Electric GE9X engines each produce about 110,000 pounds of thrust, among the most powerful commercial jet engines built, while the A380's Rolls-Royce Trent 900 and Engine Alliance GP7200 engines are typically rated at 70,000 to 84,000 pounds each. Advances in bypass ratio, materials and wing design let the 777-9 match similar missions on two engines instead of four. The figures: the A380 burns about 4,600 gallons (17,412.89 liters) of fuel per hour against about 2,600 gallons (9,842.071 liters) for the 777-9, a difference of roughly 2,000 gallons, with typical seating of about 555 and 426 respectively; Boeing claims about 10 percent lower fuel burn than the 777-300ER through the GE9X and aerodynamics. Maximum takeoff weight is 1.27 million pounds (575,000 kilograms) for the A380 and 775,000 pounds (351,500 kilograms) for the 777-9. The 777-9 also brings a high aspect-ratio composite wing, folding wingtips and a wingspan of 235 feet 5 inches (71.80 meters), improving lift-to-drag ratio and reducing induced drag.

Where the goal is moving the most passengers through a slot-constrained airport such as London Heathrow or Tokyo Narita, the A380 is still unmatched, and on a high-demand route a full A380 can be economical. But most airlines do not build fleets around a handful of peak routes; they need aircraft that earn money across varied markets, seasons and demand, and there the 777-9's lower fuel burn, lighter maintenance burden and greater flexibility outweigh its smaller cabin. In practice airlines use the 777-9 less as a one-for-one replacement for an A380 flight than as a replacement for the role the A380 played in a network: routes that fill 550 seats in July may fill only 400 in February, and the twinjet lets capacity track demand while keeping the connection. The market has voted the same way: Airbus ended A380 production in 2021 after delivering 251 aircraft and securing 251 firm orders, while the 777-9 had 546 firm orders as of September before entering service, including more than 200 777X family aircraft for Emirates. At published list prices those orders represent about $111.9 billion for the A380 and about $241.4 billion for the 777-9, though airlines rarely pay list prices.

facts.claim: Having been manufactured from 2003 until 2021, the Airbus A380 currently does not have a direct replacement available on the open market, and it is the highest capacity commercial jet ever produced, with its most dense example operated by Emirates, at 615 seats.

Airbus' official product page outlines that the A380 has a maximum certified capacity of 853 seats, while typical A380 layouts contain 500-600 seats and typical 777-9 layouts are around 400-430 seats, with more than one cabin onboard.

Flight Global reported back in 2018 that Korean Air once configured an A380 at 407 seats, in an all-business class layout, marking the lowest density example known to have flown, as a charter exception.

According to Aero Corner, the 777-9's two General Electric GE9X engines each generate roughly 110,000 pounds of thrust, while the A380's Rolls-Royce Trent 900 and Engine Alliance GP7200 engines are typically rated between 70,000 and 84,000 pounds of thrust each.

Typical fuel burn per hour is about 4,600 gallons (17,412.89 liters) for the Airbus A380 and about 2,600 gallons (9842.071 liters) for the Boeing 777-9, with typical seats of about 555 and about 426, and Boeing claims about 10% lower fuel burn than the Boeing 777-300ER through the GE9X and aerodynamics.

The A380's maximum takeoff weight is 1.27 million lb (575,000 kg), whereas the 777-9's MTOW is 775,000 lb (351,500 kg), and the 777-9 has a wingspan of 235 feet, 5 inches (71.80 meters) with a high aspect-ratio composite wing and folding wingtips.

If the objective is moving the maximum possible number of passengers through a slot-constrained airport such as London Heathrow Airport (LHR) or Tokyo Narita Airport (NRT), the A380 remains unmatched, while the 777-9's lower fuel consumption, reduced maintenance burden, and greater operational flexibility outweigh its lower seating capacity for most airlines.

Airbus ended A380 production in 2021 after delivering 251 aircraft and ultimately secured 251 firm orders for the A380, while Boeing's 777-9 had accumulated 546 firm orders as of September despite not yet entering commercial service, and Emirates alone ordered more than 200 aircraft from the 777X family.

Using each manufacturer's published list prices, the A380 order total equates to approximately $111.9 billion in potential sales revenue and roughly $241.4 billion for the 777-9 alone, while airlines rarely pay published list prices.

zh.title: 波音777-9為何無法直接取代空中巴士A380：座位數與燃油效率的取捨
zh.summary: A380於2003至2021年間生產，典型布局500至600席，至今沒有直接替代機型；777-9典型布局約400至430席，但每小時燃油消耗約2,600加侖，遠低於A380的約4,600加侖。777-9以雙發設計與較低的營運彈性取勝，取代的是A380在航網中的角色，而非逐班對等的座位數。
body: 空中巴士A380於2003至2021年間生產，是史上載客量最大的商用噴射機，至今市場上沒有可直接替代的機型。典型布局約500至600席，阿聯酋航空密度最高的配置達615席，空中巴士官方產品頁面列出的最大認證載客量為853席。最接近的後繼機型是空中巴士A350與波音777家族的高載客量版本，座位數接近但未超過500席。波音777-9的典型布局約400至430席，設有多個客艙；2018年大韓航空曾有一架A380採407席全商務艙配置，據Flight Global報導為已知密度最低的案例，但屬於特殊包機任務。無論各家航空公司如何配置，A380的機身面積與最大認證載客量都高於777-9，A380航線上的總座位數無法平均轉移到777-9。

座位數的差距由燃油效率彌補。777-9的兩具通用電氣GE9X發動機各約110,000磅推力，屬於史上推力最大的商用噴射發動機之列；A380的勞斯萊斯Trent 900與Engine Alliance GP7200發動機各約70,000至84,000磅推力。配合旁通比、材料與機翼設計的進步，777-9僅以兩具發動機即可達到相近的任務能力。數據上，A380每小時燃油消耗約4,600加侖（17,412.89公升），777-9約2,600加侖（9,842.071公升），相差約2,000加侖；典型座位數分別約555席與426席；波音公司稱777-9透過GE9X與空氣動力設計，燃油消耗較777-300ER低約10%。A380最大起飛重量127萬磅（575,000公斤），777-9為775,000磅（351,500公斤），幾近兩倍之差；777-9另有高展弦比複合材料機翼、可折疊翼尖與235英尺5英寸（71.80公尺）翼展，升阻比更佳、誘導阻力更低。

在倫敦希斯洛機場或東京成田機場等時段受限的機場，若目標是以單一航班運送最多旅客，A380仍無可匹敵；但多數航空公司並非圍繞少數高需求航線規畫機隊，而是追求在不同市場、季節與需求條件下都能獲利，777-9較低的燃油消耗、維修負擔與更高的營運彈性便逐漸勝過座位數的劣勢。實務上，航空公司往往不是以777-9逐班取代A380，而是以它取代A380在航網中扮演的角色：淡季時A380座位難以獲利售出，業者可以更精準地匹配運力與需求，同時維持航網連結。市場反應也說明了產業的轉向：A380於2021年結束生產，總計交付251架、取得251筆確認訂單；777-9雖尚未投入商業服務，截至9月已累積546筆確認訂單，阿聯酋航空一家就訂購逾200架777X家族飛機。按製造商公布的牌價計算，A380訂單總值約1,119億美元，777-9約2,414億美元；不過航空公司實際支付的價格很少等於牌價。
